clue.text: Radical doctor may take a bit of stick

indicators.note: only a bit of the word is wanted, so its tail is cut away

blocks.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
the word with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A hard-line doctor is prepared to put up with some criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of stick' reads as some criticism, but it asks for most of the word stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic and radical both describe measures that are extreme and far-reaching.

clue.text: Put off, but provide food again on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: to feed again is to refeed; past tense refed

explanation.surface: Someone delays a meal but promises to serve it again later.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer something is to postpone it, which is what putting it off means.

clue.text: Name is a difficulty when suffering memory loss

indicators.note: letters in difficulty and suffering are in a bad state, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Remembering a name is hard for someone who is losing their memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total loss of recall.

clue.text: A weeping wound?

blocks.note: first meaning: a drop shed from the eye when crying
second meaning: a rip or gash, as in a muscle

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests one oozing injury; the word is pronounced differently in each sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling names a single teardrop shed in crying and a rip or laceration in flesh.

clue.text: Great Empress comes round with fireworks

blocks.note: Catherine the Great, Empress of Russia
to wheel is to turn or circle round

explanation.surface: A grand empress arrives just as the fireworks start.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine wheels are spinning fireworks pinned to a post, named after Saint Catherine.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine wheels are rotating firework devices that spin while throwing out sparks.

clue.text: Sailor raises pile of money to pick up bird

indicators.note: lifting something up turns it over, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: Jack tar is an old name for a sailor
a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: A sailor gathers a stack of cash so he can buy a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-headed member of the crow family.

clue.text: Knave first to love autumn crafts, but he's master of none of them

definitions.text: he's master of none of them

blocks.note: the knave in a pack of cards is the jack
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
fall is the American word for autumn
skilled crafts are trades

explanation.surface: A rogue loves seasonal handicrafts yet is good at none of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the proverb 'jack of all trades, master of none'; JACK comes first, then O, FALL and TRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb describes someone who dabbles in many skills without becoming expert in any single one.

clue.text: Traditional dish made from pottage served with crushed ice

indicators.note: something crushed is broken up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned stew is oddly served with crushed ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Pottage is a thick soup or stew; cottage pie is minced beef topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is a long-established British dish of minced meat baked under mashed potato.

clue.text: Samuel Pepys was reportedly the worst

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: the most dire is the worst

explanation.surface: A slur that the famous seventeenth-century writer was the worst of men.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'direst' and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys kept a celebrated daily journal of 1660s London, making him history's best-known keeper of a diary.

clue.text: Roused by funeral party when little Dennis returned

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the short name is read backwards

blocks.note: a wake is a gathering after a funeral
Den is a short form of Dennis

explanation.surface: Someone is woken by the noise of a wake when Dennis comes home.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roused is to be woken up or stirred from sleep.

clue.text: See enthusiast with cat: it's dancing. Wonderful!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they land in a new order

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiast
the letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: An onlooker marvels at a cat-lover whose pet dances.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is an informal intensifier for something marvellous or excellent.

clue.text: Follow a trail

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to pursue or trace
second meaning: a noun, a rough path

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction to follow a trail, but the verb and the noun phrase are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to pursue someone; as a noun it means a rough path or footway.

clue.text: To start run with a broken ski is a gamble

indicators.note: a broken item has its parts out of place, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: Setting off down a slope on a damaged ski is reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a venture whose outcome is uncertain, the same thing as a gamble.

clue.text: Short Christmas-time speech provides embellishment

blocks.note: Dec is the short form of December, the Christmas month
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A brief festive address adds a flourish to the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is an ornament added to make something prettier, which is an embellishment.

clue.text: Comedians' day out produces funny graphic

blocks.note: comics are comedians
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A comedians' outing results in an amusing cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic strip is a sequence of drawn panels telling a humorous story.

clue.text: Actor takes dodgy CIA job

indicators.note: something dodgy is not straight, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer accepts a shady assignment from American intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Derek Jacobi is an English stage and screen actor, known for I, Claudius.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek Jacobi is a famous British performer, so he is an example of an actor.

clue.text: After playing Lear to a tee, Edward was warned

indicators.note: an actor playing a role reinterprets it, so the letters take new positions

blocks.note: letters as written, before rearranging
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: An actor who plays King Lear perfectly is given a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a tee' means perfectly, but here 'a tee' is just the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alerted is to be made aware of danger, the same as being warned.

clue.text: Is celibacy an ideal, or can it produce poison?

indicators.note: the phrase yields the answer from within its own run of letters

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A philosophical question: is chastity a virtue or a toxic idea?
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a fast-acting deadly chemical, the classic toxin of detective stories.

clue.text: Prince's cleaning lady meets the French

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaner
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A royal's cleaner is introduced to some French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles was the long-serving Prince of Wales, heir to the British throne.

clue.text: Mixed team go with me to river to measure the current

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the instrument that does this

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: letters as written
letters as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mixed team and I go down to the river to check its flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The current is electrical, not a river's flow, and the definition describes what the device does.
explanation.definitionFit: An ammeter is an instrument for gauging electric flow in amperes.

clue.text: Hang about! Look, it may be the Queen!

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to wait because the monarch might appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang about!' looks like an exclamation meaning 'wait', but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly somewhere, the same as hanging about.

clue.text: Go off former lover (quiet student) and overdose on Ecstasy

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
L is the learner plate
OD is the usual abbreviation for overdose
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An angry outburst at an ex and a student who has taken too much ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a British car, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Explode and go off both describe a bomb detonating, or a person losing their temper.

clue.text: Air with a most freak acidity level before

indicators.note: a freak is abnormal, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: letters as written, before rearranging
pH is the scale of acidity
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Air that had a strangely high acidity at some earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere is the envelope of gases surrounding the earth, which we breathe as air.

clue.text: Dad returned to collect notes that were copied

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: Father came back to pick up some notes that had been photocopied.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so aped means imitated or copied.

clue.text: Take bearing in English forest - it's impenetrable

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
dene is an English dialect word for a wooded valley

explanation.surface: Someone takes a compass reading inside a thick English wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A dene (or dean) is a narrow wooded valley in English place names; S goes before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense undergrowth is so thick and closely packed that it cannot be passed through.

clue.text: Smile when king falls into the drink

indicators.note: falling into something puts one inside it

blocks.note: R, rex, is Latin for king
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: People smile when a monarch tumbles into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, but here it is a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile showing the teeth.

clue.text: After a while, one's even more dead!

blocks.note: first meaning: at some time afterwards
second meaning: comparative of late, as in the late king

explanation.walkthrough: 'The late' means deceased, so a jokey comparative of it means deader still.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means subsequently; as the comparative adjective of late (deceased) it jokingly means deader.

clue.text: I wondered about getting a quilt

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone muses about whether to buy a bedcover.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick bed covering, originally stuffed with soft duck feathers.

clue.text: Takes off clothes in oriental bars

indicators.note: one item placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: to strip is to undress
E for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone undresses in nightclubs in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like drinking places but means bands of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands of colour, also called bars.

clue.text: True Church surrounded by evil and hollow rite

indicators.note: something surrounded by others is enclosed between them
a hollow word has had its middle emptied, leaving only its outside

blocks.note: sin is wickedness
CE is the Church of England
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A true church encircled by wickedness and empty ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and true both describe feelings that are genuine and honestly meant.
